title: Wallabag test can report success from a stale cached token

evidence.quote:
async def _ensure_token(self) -> str:
        """Obtain or refresh the OAuth2 access token."""
        if WallabagService._cached_token and time.time() < WallabagService._cached_token_expires_at - 60:
            return WallabagService._cached_token

reasoning: The route treats any non-throwing _ensure_token() call as a successful connection test. _ensure_token() first returns a process-wide cached token without checking whether the current DB-backed URL, client ID, username, or password match the credentials that produced that token. After a previous successful Wallabag connection, changing the stored Wallabag config to invalid credentials can still make POST /wallabag/test return {"status":"ok"} until the old token expires.
reproduction: Configure valid Wallabag credentials and call POST /api/config/wallabag/test once. Then update the Wallabag config to an invalid password or different URL and call POST /api/config/wallabag/test again before token expiry; the cached token path can return ok without exercising the new config.
recommendation: Key the cached token by the effective Wallabag configuration, clear it whenever Wallabag config changes, or make this test path force a fresh token request for the current settings.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests cover POST /wallabag/test, and the repository search did not find route-level Wallabag config tests that exercise credential changes with an existing token cache.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a test that seeds WallabagService with a cached token, changes the DB-backed Wallabag credentials, calls test_wallabag_connection, and verifies it attempts a fresh token request or returns an error for invalid current credentials.
minimumFixScope: Wallabag token cache invalidation/keying in app/services/wallabag_service.py plus the config update/test path in app/api/config.py.
